title: Tool Reference: Issuing the Upgrade Credit on a Trade-In Registration
content:
A registration under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes that has been waiting on its valuation is moved to credit issued, and the customer is given a credit they can put toward a new piece.

The credit issued is fixed only after the registration's entries carry the appraiser's valuation of the traded piece. The credit is issued only once the upgrade desk's request record carries the customer's own confirmed declaration of the value the piece was taken in at.

## What the desk does

The desk performs this action itself. The tool `issue_upgrade_credit_f63e5226` is unlocked and then called by the agent. One call moves the registration from waiting on a valuation to credit issued, writes the credit it is issued with and the value the piece was appraised at for it, makes the whole of that credit available to spend, dates the issue on the day of the call, and books the credit as a matching entry in the registration's running entries. Afterwards the registration and its entries agree on what that credit is.

## Parameters

- `credit_reference` — the reference number of the trade-in registration the credit is issued on, written on the customer's upgrade paperwork as TU- followed by six digits; it is read from the trade-in registration lookup.
- `issued_credit_amount` — the credit being issued against the traded piece, in USD to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call and makes the same figure available to spend.
- `appraised_value` — the value the traded piece was appraised at, as recorded against the registration and now written onto it, in USD to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call.

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation naming the registration reference, the credit issued in USD to 2 decimal places, the appraised value written onto the registration in USD to 2 decimal places, the reference number of the credit entry just booked and the registration's standing afterwards. A string beginning "Error" means nothing was written; any other string means the credit is issued and available to spend.
